title: Senior risk capital is repriced every month by a uniform-price auction, with no automatic rollover
content:
A.3.2.2.4.3 defines a recurring monthly market for Senior Risk Capital. The available pool (Total SRC = designated Internal SRC plus available External SRC from the srUSDS contract) "is calculated and publicly announced" before each bidding window (A.3.2.2.4.3.2). Primes then bid "(1) The quantity of SRC the Prime seeks to originate, and (2) The maximum price the Prime is willing to pay (expressed in basis points above the Base Rate)" (A.3.2.2.4.3.3).

Allocation is a textbook uniform-price auction (A.3.2.2.4.3.4): bids ranked descending by price, filled sequentially until the pool is exhausted, and "the price of the lowest successful bid that receives an allocation (even partial) sets the uniform clearing price for the month. All winning bidders pay this clearing price ... regardless of their original bid price."

The uniform-price choice matters. Under pay-as-bid, an Agent that genuinely values capital highly must shade its bid downward to avoid overpaying, and the auction stops revealing true willingness to pay. Uniform pricing makes honest bidding close to optimal, so the clearing price becomes a real market signal — the ecosystem's price of loss-absorbing capacity, denominated as a spread over the Base Rate and reset monthly.

A.3.2.2.4.3.6 refuses persistence: "OSRC is valid only for the single monthly period following the settlement cycle in which it was originated. Renewal requires successful participation in the next monthly origination process; there is no automatic rollover." Every Agent's senior capital is therefore up for competitive re-auction every month, which prevents incumbency from locking up scarce capacity — and creates a genuine monthly refinancing risk: an Agent whose positions still need senior backing may be outbid.

The same one-month horizon bounds the secondary market. A.3.2.2.4.4.1 permits sub-renting of rented OSRC if the Accord says so, but the rental period "cannot extend beyond the end of the current Monthly Settlement Cycle," so chains of sub-rentals cannot outlive the capital that backs them. A.3.2.2.4.4.2 adds that rented OSRC still has to be SPJ-enabled by the borrower's own junior capital, or it does not count.
description: Primes bid quantity and a maximum price in basis points over the Base Rate; the lowest successful bid sets one clearing price for all winners, and allocated capital is valid for a single month.
